findings.text: follow-on: the plan names the three direct callers of derived_plan_age in tests/test_doccheck.py (lines 124,135,150) as callers that must pass the new arguments, but they were left unchanged, so only the fallback chain (plan-modified, file-created, file-mtime) is exercised and the new last-commit-first branch has no test at this level; low severity - the fallback tests remain correct and the plan's own new module covers the new branch end to end, but the node did not do what the plan wrote.

follow-on: the functional change in this file is _authorisation_age routing through repo_dir/docs_dir, but ~8 additional hunks are formatting-only (import reordering and collapsed conditionals across _plan_dependency_satisfied, _plan_dependency_judgment, sprint_summary_rows, _drift_is_member_progress, target_row, _judgment_member, _gate_section_edges); the repo rule asks that mechanical reformatting not be folded into a feature change because it hides the intended change from a reviewer.

follow-on: the AGING/STALE boundary at exactly 30 days is untested: the new test covers 20 (AGING) and 40 (STALE) only, and the split depends on lifecycle_staleness returning stale only for age_days > ACTIVE_PLAN_STALE_AFTER_DAYS; a plan at exactly 30 days is reported AGING, which matches the plan's 'past 30 days STALE', but no test pins the boundary.

follow-on: the test asserts both _age_of(fixture date) and a literal 20 (40 for the stale plan); the plan's done-when says the ages are derived from the fixture's own dates never written as literals. justifications.evidence: I reran the named gate at head c597bb999 in the reviewed worktree (118 passed EXIT=0, review-gate-head.log with a header naming revision/tree/command) and independently reproduced the negative control in a scratch export with the commit lookup disabled (_plan_last_committed returns None), where both tests fail with KeyError('aging','AGING') at EXIT=1 (review-negctl.log), so the guard fires under mutation as the reviewed run claims. justifications.fit: the change edits existing readers in place and routes them through the existing owner rather than adding a reader; the new _plan_last_committed is named by what it does, AGING joins the existing SEVERITIES/flag_order scheme, and the message carries a conventional subject with a body and no AI attribution.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deliverable lands: derived_plan_age now reads the last one first through the existing _git_last_committed whole-tree map, keyed by the plan path made relative to the repo, falling back to plan-modified, created, then mtime; the audit loop, roadmap's _authorisation_age and archive's find_archive_candidates all pass repo_dir/docs_dir and every finding carries age_source; the AGING band (active, impl<1.0, age 14..30) sits before STALE (>30) with no overlap because lifecycle_staleness returns stale only past 30. justifications.reuse: derived_plan_age stays the single age owner and the new source reuses serve._git_last_committed - the whole-tree map the server already builds - rather than a new git reader; _plan_last_committed is a thin path lookup over that map, and the existing _parse_last_committed/_GitCreationEntry cache is reused unchanged.
justifications.scope_discipline: the change is confined to the declared write paths plus one evidence fragment, all inside the section's fence, and nothing outside is modified; the naming and attribution checks over the added lines and the message body are clean. Docked for two reasons: the declared write path tests/test_doccheck.py is untouched, so a named deliverable is left undone rather than deferred; and the roadmap.py diff folds ~8 formatting-only hunks (import reordering and collapsed conditionals in _plan_dependency_satisfied, _plan_dependency_judgment, sprint_summary_rows, _drift_is_member_progress, target_row, _judgment_member, _gate_section_edges) into the functional change, which the repo rule discourages - mechanical reformatting mixed with intent is what makes both unreviewable.
